Still haven't addressed a single point I made about the pros of a merger, but I'll address these points anyway.

$TSLA is up 250% over the past 6 years, so the opposite of flat.

Cars that drive themselves are indisputably already here, not a 5+ year promise. Tesla is currently offering unsupervised rides via Robotaxi, with Cybercab in production since April and added to the Robotaxi fleet earlier this month.

Billions of robots will be at least 5 years out, agreed on that point. BUT once Tesla reaches volume Optimus production in 1-2 years (factory is already being built), the markets will price in that growth well before we see billions delivered.

For SpaceX specifically, going from negative ~$2B to negative ~$150M GAAP operating income in one quarter while almost doubling capex is extremely bullish and indicates a very short time horizon to real value. Currently, this is driven by profit-making revenue from Starlink and selling compute to the hyperscalers and frontier AI labs. Long-term, the gap will only widen once Starship enables extremely cheap and frequent Starlink V3 launches combined with space-based AI compute/model revenue. AI satellites will start launching next year.

When making comments on these companies' capex, it's important to remember that they're undertaking nation-scale infrastructure buildouts at a rate never before seen in history to accomplish tasks never accomplished in history. Tesla is doing this profitably, and SpaceX soon will be too. Both stocks are massively discounted at the moment relative to their medium-to-long term value.

A global study reveals an alarming accountability gap inside enterprises deploying AI, while sovereign nations double down on open-weight compliance models.

Here are the key governance and compliance updates unfolding right now:

🧠 IBM Study Highlights Systemic AI Accountability Gaps
Research from the IBM Institute for Business Value surveying CHROs and employees worldwide found that while 71% of HR chiefs believe supervising and overriding AI outputs is the most critical workforce competency, only 29% of employees value validation judgment. More critically, nearly half of organizations fail to involve HR executives when designing AI strategy. Enterprise compliance auditors are warning that unchecked agentic rollouts without clear human validation boundaries create severe liability and regulatory non-compliance risks. Read the study findings: https://t.co/K8gi2oaud8

🌐 Open-Weight Models Power 56% of Sovereign AI Initiatives
Counterpoint Research’s 2026 Sovereign AI Index reveals that 56% of sovereign AI models are adapted from open-source bases (dominated by Meta's Llama family), rather than closed commercial APIs. National governments and regulated industries are choosing open architectures to maintain strict data residency, control model weights, and adhere to domestic privacy and cybersecurity mandates. Read the index report: https://t.co/GRXB6KVDfA

🏛️ EU AI Board Moves into Enforcement Mode
Following its September meeting, the European Union AI Board is transitioning into direct supervisory enforcement under the EU AI Act. Regulators are prioritizing Article 50 transparency obligations and assessing Member State sandbox deployments to ensure high-risk automated tools maintain auditable human-override controls. Read the regulatory update: https://t.co/JfBY7XNect

**Builder Takeaway:**
Automated tools are only as safe as the human validation workflows built around them. By embedding explicit human-in-the-loop review gates, audit-logged overrides, and open-weight data controls, you protect your software from enterprise liability and regulatory enforcement.

How is your organization enforcing human validation and auditability across automated AI workflows? Let's discuss in the comments below! 👇

One of the reasons I long wanted to start @PractiveSec was because of the fact that the cyber security industry had turned from the truth, abandoned its mission, and had become a whore for the money laundering schemes of Silicon Valley. 

Far too often I would leave meetings with CEOs and founders and Presidents angry and insulted by their prolific and bold lying. The deep wokeness, hypocrisy, hatred, and flat-out lying made every day difficult to endure. Silicon Valley is a pit of grime and muck that loves power and money. The current CEO of Palo Alto Networks used to brag to employees that he didn’t care about cyber security at all. The President at CrowdStrike has so many faces and lies so profusely, I wonder if he can even see. I wonder if he even can tell the truth.

This past week, I’ve been pouring over the AI-powered cyber attack reports, and looking at how the so-called leaders of cyber security are responding. True to kind, they are chasing the money, truth be damned. All that matters is company growth.

I want to help organizations wade through this and focus on the truth and what is actually needed to solve the real problems. 

Right now the marketing and product strategy teams of the cyber world are attaching themselves to the AI hype like a leech. They are letting the false narrative of OpenAI and Anthropic lead, while they take in new cash and customers via product and service strategies that drain the resources of their customers while adding a heavy burden to them.

I hate it. I hate the lies and those who allow the lies because they can sell on them.

I’m writing as fast as I can, but hear me: fundamentals work. They still work in the face of AI powered attacks. You don’t need more tech. You need to apply the fundamentals.
